title: "Rules"

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_docs.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

`run` and `sync` refuse a recipe that breaks one of these rules, before changing anything on disk, and `check` reports it as `refused`. A refusal names the rule; from Python, `RecipeRefused.rule` is its number. On the command line: `useful-views rules`.

## Rule 1: recipe.toml is complete

recipe.toml exists and can be read. It has a one-sentence description that does not start with TODO, and inputs and outputs, each a list of at least one path with no path listed twice.

## Rule 2: Steps are numbered and described

The recipe has at least one step file named NN_name.py. Each starts with a # comment saying what it does, not starting with TODO, and no two steps share a number.

## Rule 3: Steps are Python files

No file in the recipe folder is named like a step in another language (.R, .Rmd, .ipynb, .qmd, .jl, .do).

## Rule 4: Inputs exist and are allowed

Each input is a file under raw/ or directly inside useful-views/, written relative to the project root with forward slashes, and exists with exactly that letter case. A raw input is not empty and can be read.

## Rule 5: Input views come from a recipe that has run

An input inside useful-views/ is an output of another recipe, and that recipe has run successfully.

## Rule 6: No cycles

The recipe does not read its own view, directly or through a chain of other recipes.

## Rule 7: Outputs are allowed and unique

Each output is a .parquet file directly inside useful-views/, is not useful-views/README.md, and is not made by another recipe.

## Rule 8: Resource names are unique

No two recorded files share a resource name: the file name without its extension, lowercased, with characters other than a-z, 0-9, '.', '_' and '-' turned into '-'.

A recipe name that does not match a folder in `recipes/`, or a folder name that is not allowed, is also refused, with `rule` set to `None`.
